findings.text: Jeremiah 22:16–17: knowing God, said as doing justice for the poor. *The largest gap.*: > "He judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it was well. Is not this to know me? declares the; > Lord. But you have eyes and heart only for your dishonest gain, for shedding innocent blood, and for; > practicing oppression and violence."; The passage (22:13–17) sets Josiah against his son, who builds "by unrighteousness" and makes his; neighbour work unpaid. God himself calls judging the poor's cause *knowing me*. The son's eyes and; heart are given "only" to gain. This is an inner-being statement in God's own words:

findings.text: Job 31:16–17: the poor's desire not withheld.: > "If I have withheld anything that the poor desired, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail, or; > have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it"; These are Job's own words, in the oath God's verdict supports (Job 42:7). Here the M18 word is the; poor man's own desire, which Job swears he did not refuse. "Eaten my morsel alone" names the act of; not sharing. 10.10 already has 31:19–20 from the same oath, and this sits just before it.

Mark 14:4–7: the poor as a pretext, and doing good "whenever you want".: > "There were some who said to themselves indignantly, 'Why was the ointment wasted like that? For; > this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.' And; > they scolded her. But Jesus said, 'Leave her alone … For you always have the poor with you, and; > whenever you want, you can do good for them. But you will not always have me.'"; Mark gives what Matthew does not: the indignation was "to themselves" first, then spoken as a scolding.; Jesus' answer puts doing good to the poor in the hearers' own will ("whenever you want"). The poor are; named in the scolding. Jesus answers it, and the verses do not say what lay behind it in Mark. John; 12:6 says it of Judas, but John 12 is not in this set.

findings.text: Ecclesiastes 9:15–16: the poor wise man forgotten and not heard.: > "But there was found in it a poor, wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city. Yet no one; > remembered that poor man. But I say that wisdom is better than might, though the poor man's wisdom; > is despised and his words are not heard."; What seeing someone poor did here: he was not remembered, and his words not heard, though he; had saved the city. This bears on 10.3 (forgetting) and 10.2 (hearing).
For M18 itself: nothing missing. Where the M18 word carries the act (Pro 22:9, Mat 19:21, Rom: 15:26–27), the verse is already told. Where the word is a qualifier, the act lies elsewhere.
